items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'Tunger's singing' in the context of a song title, but Interviewee does not mention Tunger or indicate any personal interaction.

ctx.x: Mm-hm- I was trying to think, it was far back, old numbers you know. Pete called Sonora, beautiful number. Was that a tango? Something like that.

You know what that's called? That's called the Egyptian fantasy. That's what Bechet called the Egyptian fantasy, that Tunger's singing. What he called it now? Da-dee-dee-do-dee-dee-da-da. He called the Egyptian. Isn't that the Egyptian? Egyptian. That's the middle part, that's the bridge. No, no, no, no. That's the Egyptian, isn't it? Yeah. It's a beautiful tune.

After the dance, we used to play a piece called Get Outta Here. Da-da-da. Da-da-da. Da-da-da. Da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. Get outta here. And gone home. See, the Lory went to work. What did he make out of that? What do you call it now? He does it.
